newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bomb explodes outside Norwegian bikers' building.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes outside Norwegian bikers' building.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded outside the Oslo headquarters of a Norwegian motorcycle gang early on Wednesday in what appeared to be the latest incident in a Nordic biker war, police said.
Nobody was injured in the explosion, which shattered windows in the building and damaged a wall in a neighbouring house, said the national news agency NTB.
The bomb exploded beneath a stolen car parked outside the headquarters of MC Norway, a group aspiring to become members of the Hell's Angels. The car was destroyed.
Police spokesman Knut Mikkelsen said authorities believed the attack was the work of the rival Bandidos gang.
"We base this suspicion on the fact that a biker war has been going on for some time in the Nordic (countries)," he told national radio.
NTB said police were looking for two men who were seen outside the building by MC Norway members. Five people were in the building at the time of the attack, it said.
Violence between the Hell's Angels and the Bandidos -- both Nordic offshoots of U.S. motorcycle clans -- flared in 1994 when a Hell's Angel member was murdered in Helsingborg in Sweden.
Several other bikers have been killed since then. The most recent incident was three weeks ago when two people died in an attack on a Copenhagen building used by Hell's Angels.

In Denmark, a series of attacks on biker premises in urban areas has led to growing pressure by residents to force the gangs out of town centres to areas where there is less danger of innocent bystanders being caught in the crossfire.
